cdp:st:D.1.9:
\begin{proposition}\label{cdp:st:D.1.9}
\StatementRecord{cdp:st:D.1.9}{proved}{Historical records: GPT-6 Astra (OpenAI, ChatGPT Pro mode), effort Pro, 17 November 2026; Claude Fable 5.2 (Anthropic), effort high, 16 November 2026. Also checked in this writing by \CurrentChecker. The transgression, coherent lift, irrational unitary character, and the passage to all Picard components by a finite power were re-derived}{the hypotheses, notation and definitions stated here; \cref{cdp:eq:D5}; \cref{cdp:st:D.1.8}; \cref{cdp:st:D.1.7}}

Let $Y$ be a connected compact complex manifold with
$b_1(Y)=b_2(Y)=0$, and let $f:Y\to\PP^1$ be a proper
holomorphic surjection with connected fibres. There is a class
$\beta\in H^1(Y,\OO_Y)$ such that, for every irrational real number
$r$, the line bundle
\[
L_r=\exp(2\pi i\,r\beta)
\]
has infinite order on every scheme-theoretic fibre of $f$.
Every connected component of $\Pic(Y)$ likewise contains a real
one-parameter family with this property at every irrational real
parameter.
No local-freeness assumption on $R^1f_*\OO_Y$ or constant-dimension
assumption on fibre cohomology is required.
\end{proposition}
night:P4.26:
\begin{proposition}[P4.26]\label{night:P4.26}\label{stmt:P4.26}
\StatementRecord{night:P4.26}{proved}{The night-run re-derivation was by GPT-6 Astra (OpenAI, ChatGPT Pro mode, effort Pro), 16--18 November 2026. Also checked in this writing by \CurrentChecker. The rational pole-support transfers, conductor pushout and group presentations, class-VII alternatives, local ruled and Hopf comparisons, normal cover case, Euler sum and parity were re-derived with the source's exact separation between the single-support conclusion and the global all-support hypothesis}{\ref{night:P4.12}; \ref{night:P4.13}; \ref{night:P4.21}; \ref{night:P4.23}; \ref{night:P4.25}; \ref{night:P4.6}; \ref{night:P4.7}; \ref{night:P4.8}; \ref{night:P4R.1}; \ref{night:P4R.6}; \ref{night:P4R.7}; \ref{night:P4R.8}; \ref{night:P4R.9}}

In Part~4.2 every irreducible reduced fibre support
has nonnegative topological Euler number. For a
singular irreducible support, rational resolution
of the normalization gives strictly positive
Euler number; so does a resolution whose minimal
model is of class VII with positive second
Betti number. These assertions permit singular
normalization.

Every normal-crossing support has the
nonnegative even Euler number of P4.6.
Consequently, for a fibration all of whose
reduced supports are irreducible or have
normal crossings,
\[
 B=\mathbb P^1,\qquad c_3(Y)\in\{0,2\},
 \qquad b_3(Y)=2-c_3(Y).
\]
This last conclusion does not assume a
classification of the equality cases for
irreducible nonnormal supports.
\end{proposition}
night:P4.32:
\begin{proposition}[P4.32]\label{night:P4.32}\label{stmt:P4.32}
\StatementRecord{night:P4.32}{proved}{The night-run re-derivation was by GPT-6 Astra (OpenAI, ChatGPT Pro mode, effort Pro), 16--18 November 2026. Also checked in this writing by \CurrentChecker. The zero-Euler normalization and conductor alternatives were checked against their stated local inputs. The local conclusion uses the single support, ambient b1=b2=0, and nearby tori; the final global assertion retains the source hypothesis that every support is irreducible or NC}{\ref{night:P4.12}; \ref{night:P4.22}; \ref{night:P4.24}; \ref{night:P4.26}; \ref{night:P4.27}; \ref{night:P4.29}; \ref{night:P4.31}; \ref{night:P4.8}; \ref{night:P4R.11}; \ref{night:P4R.7}; \ref{night:P4R.9}}

An irreducible support in Part~4.2 has Euler number zero exactly
in the following cases: it is smooth with a finite unramified
torus cover, or it is singular with smooth minimal elliptic ruled
normalization, or it is singular with smooth minimal Hopf
normalization. In the ruled double-horizontal case the conductor
image is a smooth elliptic curve; the local germs are product
cusps, product tacnodes, or product ordinary plane triple points,
and the reduced conductor maps have degrees one, two, or three
respectively and are unramified.

For a fibration whose supports are all irreducible or normal
crossing, $c_3(Y)=0$ exactly when every irreducible support has
one of these forms and every reducible support has the
zero-Euler normal-crossing form of P4.8.
\end{proposition}
cdp:st:C.2.MH.1:
\begin{proposition}[The analytic support comparison used here]\label{cdp:st:C.2.MH.1}
\StatementRecord{cdp:st:C.2.MH.1}{proved}{Historical records: GPT-6 Astra (OpenAI, ChatGPT Pro mode), effort Pro, 17 November 2026; Claude Fable 5.2 (Anthropic), effort high, 16 November 2026. Also checked in this writing by \CurrentChecker. The quotient logarithmic complex, local residues, support cone, and support-to-restriction map were re-derived. Steenbrink 1999 section 3 Theorem 1 and Corollary 2 and section 4 equation (3) were opened. Its algebraic-ambient hypothesis is replaced here by an explicit construction on compact projective strata; finite characters and degree-one trace were checked separately}{the hypotheses, notation and definitions stated here; \cref{cdp:eq:C.MH.2}; \cite[Section~3, Theorem~1 and
Corollary~2]{Steenbrink1999}; \cite[Section~4, equation~(3)]{Steenbrink1999}; \cref{cdp:eq:C.MH.3}; \cref{cdp:eq:C.MH.5}}

Let $U$ be a smooth complex threefold, let $S\subset U$ be a
compact divisor, and suppose that an embedded resolution
$r:U'\to U$ is a sequence of blowups with smooth compact
centres in $S$, with $D=(r^{-1}S)_{\rm red}$ a simple
normal crossings divisor whose components are projective.
Let $V$ be a finite-monodromy rational local system on $U$.
Suppose that the cohomology of the punctured sufficiently
small fibre tubes around $S$, with coefficients in $V$,
vanishes in every degree. Then the mixed Hodge structure
on $H^k(S,V)$ obtained from a projective hyperresolution
is pure of weight $k$.

In this assertion the support-to-restriction morphism is
the actual morphism
\[
 R\Gamma_D(U',r^*V)\longrightarrow
 \underset{D\subset W}{\mathop{\rm colim}}\,
 R\Gamma(W,r^*V)=R\Gamma(D,r^*V).
 \tag{C.MH.1}\label{cdp:eq:C.MH.1}
\]
Neither a K\"ahler metric on $U$ nor a projective
compactification of $U$ is needed for this comparison.
\end{proposition}
cdp:st:C.2.MH.2:
\begin{proposition}[Euler number from a ruled normalization]\label{cdp:st:C.2.MH.2}
\StatementRecord{cdp:st:C.2.MH.2}{proved}{Historical records: GPT-6 Astra (OpenAI, ChatGPT Pro mode), effort Pro, 17 November 2026; Claude Fable 5.2 (Anthropic), effort high, 16 November 2026. Also checked in this writing by \CurrentChecker. The self-dual finite-character augmentation system, torus Koszul acyclicity, support duality, conductor weight separation, negative-definite exceptional Gysin map, and formula d e(S)=2h4(Z,V)-h3(Z,V) were re-derived. This gives 2 in the rational case and 2-2g in the ruled case}{the hypotheses, notation and definitions stated here; \cref{cdp:st:D.1.9}; \cref{cdp:st:D.1.8}; \cref{cdp:st:C.2.MH.1}; \cref{cdp:eq:C.MH.9}; \cref{cdp:eq:C.MH.8}; \cref{cdp:eq:C.MH.13}; \cref{cdp:eq:C.MH.11}; \cref{cdp:eq:C.MH.14}}

Let $f:Y\to\PP^1$ satisfy the full CDP hypotheses
$b_1(Y)=b_2(Y)=0$ with smooth torus general fibre.
Let $mS$ be a full fibre with irreducible reduced support,
and let $Z\to T\to S$ be a resolution of its
normalization. If $Z$ is rational, then
\[
                              e(S)=2.
 \tag{C.MH.6}\label{cdp:eq:C.MH.6}
\]
If $Z$ is ruled over a curve of genus $g\ge1$, then
\[
                              e(S)=2-2g.
 \tag{C.MH.7}\label{cdp:eq:C.MH.7}
\]
The calculation retains all multiplicities in the full
fibre and places no normal crossings assumption on $S$.
\end{proposition}
